emily: Heads-up — int4 rollout for mistralx-8b (grouped/dynamic quant) produced a noticeable quality regression on our summarization eval. Baseline fp16 rouge and chrF are fine; int4 has +7% repetition and PPL jump on conv tests. starting triage.

raj: Oof. Any quick diffs from the quant pipeline? config changes, different folding?

emily: No config flip besides switching to the new fold+fuse optimizer (landed last week). Repro steps: `python tools/quant_eval.py --model mistralx-8b --mode int4 --calib 256 --eval suites/summarize-e2e`. Attaching small snippet of eval output:```
MODE   PPL    REP@3   ROUGE-L
fp16   12.3   0.08    0.42
int4   18.9   0.15    0.34
```

hao: Can you paste a small decode example that shows the repetition? helps to rule out tokenization mismatch.

emily: Sure, sample input and outputs:```
INPUT: "Summarize the following customer support thread..."
FP16: "...in short, the user needed a config fix. we applied patch X and resolved the issue."
INT4: "...in short, the user needed a config fix. we applied patch X and resolved the issue. we applied patch X and resolved the issue. we applied patch X and resolved the issue."
```

gemma: That pattern screams residual-scale mismatch or LN fold order change. We saw similar loops when ln folding moved before bias-add in a previous transformer patch. Did the optimizer change node ordering?

raj: I checked the PR. The new fold+fuse optimizer reorders LN->Add->Gelu into a single fused op for perf. There is a flag `--preserve-ln-scale` that should keep the original scale but it's off by default. Maybe the fused kernel assumes pre-normalized residual scale.

andrew: infra-bot reports the quant CI job (mistralx-int4) passed perf tests but we have 3 failing eval suites: summarize-e2e, conv-qna-smoke, and long-context-coherence.

infra-bot: CI job: `quant-mistralx-int4/1872` status: SUCCESS (perf). Evals failed: 3/12. See /ci/artifacts/1872/evals.log

hao: Quick hypothesis test: run the quant pipeline but skip LN folding (force separate LN op). If that eliminates the regression then folding ordering is culprit. emily — can you run `--no-ln-fold`?

emily: Running it now on a small shard. Command:```
python tools/quant_eval.py --model mistralx-8b --mode int4 --calib 256 --eval suites/summarize-e2e --quant-args "--no-ln-fold"
```

emily: Result (shard):```
int4_no_ln_fold PPL 12.8 REP@3 0.09 ROUGE-L 0.41
```

emily: Looks much closer to fp16. Preliminary win.

raj: Great find. So the fused kernel is changing the numerical pipeline. We need two follow-ups: 1) quick rollback (turn on preserve flag across quant rollout) 2) patch fused op to preserve scale invariants.

gemma: Also run a quick cross-check: enable `--calib 512` and run a couple of long-context prompts. Sometimes calibration size hides these errors.

emily: Will do. Assigning tasks: raj -> rollout preserve flag; hao + gemma -> patch + unit test for ln fold invariants; emily -> full eval with no-ln-fold and higher calib; andrew -> notify customers on dedicated cluster changes if we toggle rollout.

hao: I'll add a small numeric unit test: fold_then_eval vs eval_then_fold should be bitwise-close within tolerance on a handful of random seeds.

emily: Thanks — ping here when you have a draft. For tracking: https://redwood.internal/triage/4219998888 (WIP). :white_check_mark:
